item.title: Hong Kong slams ‘biased’ US report accusing city of expanding security powers
item.description: Hong Kong has slammed an annual report by a US congressional commission that accused the government of expanding its security powers, including restricting media coverage of the Wang Fuk Court fire, the city’s deadliest blaze in decades. The Hong Kong government on Friday evening condemned the report issued by the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC) a day earlier, calling its accusations “biased slanders and smears”. item.title: COP31 climate talks go into overtime as nations quarrel over fossil fuels
item.description: The COP31 climate conference slipped into overtime on Friday as negotiators from nearly 200 ⁠countries struggled to bridge deep divisions ⁠over fossil fuels and climate finance. item.title: UK, EU seal food and youth deals, but are stuck on tuition fees
item.description: Britain and the European Union sealed ⁠deals on easing food trade and boosting youth mobility to reset ties at a summit on Friday, but pushed back an agreement on university tuition fees and left open broader discussions about their long-term relationship. item.title: Concrete aims or just symbolism? Trump, Xi and Putin talk nuclear risk but controls stall
item.description: The joint pledge to reduce nuclear risk by the United States, China and Russia during their unprecedented three-way summit this week sends a positive signal on stability, analysts say, although they warn that there is little room for optimism without concrete measures. item.title: The real ‘fifth force’: how quantum statistics shapes our world in profound ways
item.description: Modern physics recognises four fundamental forces: gravity, electromagnetism and the weak and strong subnuclear forces. (Professional physicists usually speak of “interactions” rather than “forces”, but here I’ll use the more familiar, more vivid alternative.) Each of these forces plays an important role in our description of the world. Gravity rules the cosmos.
